session_title: Purchase medicine and nursing supplies for almonds.

content.text: Pingfan, Xingren's test results are out, and the vet recommended some medications and care supplies. I made a list, but I'm not sure where to buy them reliably. Do you have any recommended online pet pharmacies?
Let me search for you. I remember last time when we took Xingren to the vet, you mentioned that pet hospital fees are high, and online channels might be more convenient.
Found a JD store ranking list, and the top-rated ones have good reviews. You can take a look for reference.

Thank you! This list is very practical; I was just wondering how to choose. Besides medications, do you have any recommendations for care supplies like Elizabethan collars to prevent scratching wounds and affected areas?
This Elizabethan collar was used by my friend's cat, and the feedback is that the material is comfortable and doesn't hinder the cat's movement. You might want to consider it.

Looks good, almonds might be a better fit. By the way, what about hypoallergenic prescription food? The vet suggested switching diets, but I’m worried about making the wrong choice and worsening the allergies.
Hypoallergenic food does require careful consideration. I looked it up, and both Royal Canin and another brand have related products, but it's best to choose based on Almond's specific allergens.
This is the introduction to the Royal Canin Hypoallergenic Prescription Diet. What do you think? I previously shared Almond's dietary list in our history, which might be of some reference value.

The Royal brand has a decent reputation, but you need to carefully check the ingredient list. As we discussed last time when talking about health, systematic management is important—don’t blindly follow trends.

Here's the promotion for another hypoallergenic food option, which is more affordable. However, when you helped me plan the almond treatment before, you emphasized efficiency, so I'm concerned that cheaper might not mean better quality.

Promotions are worth paying attention to, but the core focus should be on ingredients and reviews. I recommend taking your time to compare options and consider the results of allergen tests, as this will save you both worry and effort.

You're right, maintaining a decent balance is important; we shouldn't compromise quality just to save money. As for the items on the medication list, it should be fine if I buy them from the store you recommended, right?

Well, the credibility of the shops on the list is relatively high. I remember last time we arranged a meal, you emphasized a quiet environment. When choosing a shop, it’s the same—check more reviews to avoid pitfalls.
Okay, I'll carefully screen them. Thanks to your help this time, you've been very supportive since Xingren fell ill. I'm truly grateful.
There's no need to be polite between friends. Xingren has recovered, so we can continue to meet up for meals, just like last time at the Sichuan restaurant—let's keep it relaxed.
Yes, health comes first. I plan to place an order for the items on the list today. I'll buy the medicine from the recommended store, and I'll compare the collar and cat food a bit more.
Okay, feel free to ask me anytime. Stay efficient and don’t let this take up too much time, so it doesn’t affect your work-life balance.
Understood, I'll arrange everything. This collaborative shopping went quite smoothly; we've confirmed the channels and the list, so Almond's treatment should proceed more smoothly.
Well, it's all about problem-solving. I hope Xingren gets better soon so we can continue to vent about workplace health issues.
Haha, definitely! The list is all set. I'll go place the order now, and we can chat later.
